exposure: Hospital structural characteristics (e.g., Baby-friendly Hospital Initiative status, special accommodations for high-risk women/newborns, separate rooms for pre-labor/vaginal delivery, rooming-in)
Hospital care practices (e.g., skin-to-skin contact adoption, presence and involvement of obstetrics nurses, charging for companions)
outcome: Prevalence of Baby-friendly Hospital Initiative status
Prevalence of special accommodations for high-risk pregnant women, mothers, and newborns
Prevalence of separate rooms for pre-labor and vaginal delivery
Number and proportion of obstetrics nurses
Proportion of vaginal deliveries assisted by obstetrics nurses
cohort: The study included 97 teaching hospitals participating in the Projeto de Aprimoramento e Inovacao no Cuidado e Ensino em Obstetricia e Neonatologia (Apice ON) project.
finding: Before the Apice ON project implementation, the participating teaching hospitals exhibited varied adherence to recommended obstetric and neonatal care practices, with only 66% being Baby-friendly, 3% offering special accommodations, and an average cesarean section rate of 42%.
mod_finding: The average cesarean section rate across the participating hospitals was 42%, ranging from 37.6% (Southeast) to 49.1% (Northeast).
